column1: # The gate's wall clock, one row per CI job: what each job costs, and the most it may cost.
# Five tab-separated columns. `seconds` and `floor` are the reference the verify job's advisory
# report compares a median of main runs against; `budget` is the ceiling a single run of the job is
# held to, and the run that breaks it is red; `measured` is that row's population -- the runs its
# own figures were taken over, as `<runs>@<date of the newest>`, and `/<run id>` after it where they
# are the attempts of one pull-request run. `-` is a column that does not apply to the row, never a
# zero.
# Updated by hand, never by the workflow: `scripts/checks/check_gate_budget.py` under `--stamp` cuts
# a row from the saved runs it is named, by the rules below, and a person commits what it proposes.
# A report that recomputed its reference from its own recent past would let a slowdown become the
# new normal one window at a time, and the accumulated growth would never appear in any single
# report.
# Population: the runs a row's stamp counts, which is the one place it is written -- completed
# pushes to main, or the attempts of one pull-request run re-run whole. Every attempt of that run
# tests its merge commit, the tree main carries once it lands if main has not moved since, so a row
# is cut before the merge from the code being merged rather than after it from code already holding
# the gate. Left out of a row's population, that row alone: a job that did not succeed; a job whose
# log carries the runner's own retry of an action download, a wait that is GitHub's rather than the
# tree's; and for a job whose own cache is keyed on the tree
# (`scripts/checks/check_gate_budget.py :: TREE_KEYED`), every attempt but the first of a push to
# main, and any pull-request run: a re-run restores everything its first attempt wrote, while a push
# to main finds warm only what the trees before it left unchanged, so re-runs read at least as warm
# as the pushes the report compares and never colder.
# A stamp counts at least ten runs. Each job gets a machine of its own, of a fast or a slow class no
# log names; read off the binding unit's timing, the slow class ran 61-76 percent of the `backend`,
# `db` and `scripts` jobs of the 33 pull-request runs of 2026-10-06, so ten runs leave it out of at
# most about one population in ten thousand, and one that leaves it out sets a budget that class
# breaks. A row whose stamp counts fewer is due a re-cut.
# Seconds: the median first-step-to-last-step span over the row's population; `-` under the
# twenty-four runs its floor needs, which leave the fast class, 24-39 percent of those jobs, out of
# at most about one population in seven hundred.
# Floor: how far a 12-run median moves at p95, in percent of the reference beside it rather than in
# seconds -- the nearest-rank p95 of how far one window's median sits from the other's, over draws
# of two disjoint windows of twelve out of the row's population, rounded up to a whole percent and
# seeded per row so a re-cut reads the same floor
# (`scripts/checks/check_gate_budget.py :: window_moves`). A row's spans are drawn alone rather than
# whole runs: one run's jobs run on separate machines, and over those 33 runs two units of one job
# moved together, a rank correlation of 0.96, where two jobs of one run did not, -0.28 to 0.15.
# A job with no row here is not compared: the report lists it under "Measured with no
# reference to compare against", the same line a row carrying `-` puts its job on
# (`scripts/checks/check_gate_budget.py :: report_window`), and the budget check fails the run that
# carries it (`:: check_run`). p95 rather than p90 because a report holding no verdict is worth
# only what it is worth reading, and a floor speaking on half of the quiet pushes spends exactly
# that.
# Budget: the highest single-run span in the stamped population, plus a quarter of it or ten
# seconds, whichever is more, rounded up to the next five. A single run swings far wider than a
# median does -- `ops` reached 1.9 times its median inside its stamped runs, `frontend` 1.5 times
# -- so a ceiling that never cries wolf on a quiet runner sits well above the reference, and a run
# over it is a re-run or a regression, in that order. Raising one costs the runs that justify it: a
# budget, a reference or a floor that rises against main carries a new stamp, a new stamp counts the
# runs its figures need, and a pull-request run stamps no job whose cache is keyed on the tree, each
# refused otherwise by `scripts/checks/check_gate_budget.py :: check_raise` in the pull request's
# `docs` job. Lowering one is free.
# A check joining the gate records its measured cost here, the **gate** clause in
# `.claude/rules/ops.md` being what asks for it. Only a new job is refused without a row; a check
# joining an existing job is held by review and by that job's budget, no step being measured alone. A cost that sits inside its job's floor moves
# neither the reference nor the budget and takes no stamp of its own. A row carrying `-` for its
# reference and floor has no floor to sit inside: the report lists its job as measured rather than
# comparing it (`scripts/checks/check_gate_budget.py :: report_window`), so a cost joining it is
# recorded with its measured figure, moves no figure, and answers to the budget alone, which holds
# every run of the job (`:: check_run`). A row with no budget either, as `images` is, has nothing
# here that judges a cost.
# `images` is measured and not budgeted: its span is the layer cache's before it is the tree's, and
# inside the population its stamp counts its widest run costs five times its narrowest, so the
# number a ceiling would be set from says more about which layers were warm than about the tree. The
# Dockerfile change most worth catching is the one that empties that cache, and the median report
# is the only guard a row like this has, so it has none while the row carries no reference.
# `backend`, `db`, `docs`, `format`, `frontend`, `images` and `scripts` are cut from the main push
# runs their stamps count, every one of them carrying the backend's tier over workers and the db
# scope's two suites started together. The `frontend-units` shards are cut from the pull-request
# run their stamp counts, named in the commit that set it: main carries no run of the tree they are
# cut for. A population as short as theirs
# cannot be cut into two windows of twelve, and drawn with replacement it reads its own smallness
# rather than the job -- five runs of `frontend` answered 5 percent that way. A floor cut before
# these jobs took their present shape measures a gate they are not, as the `ops` paragraph below
# says of a run from before its merge, and a reference with no floor beside it is a median the
# report cannot judge. So each of these rows carries `-` for both, is held by its budget alone where
# it has one, and is listed by the report as measured rather than compared; its reference and floor
# are cut once twenty-four runs of its population exist.
# `ops` answers to the main push runs to 2026-09-07 its own stamp counts, fewer than the 24 that
# end on that day: `nginx/edge_test.sh` joined that scope partway through those 24, and a run from
# before that merge measures a gate this one is not. A population that short cannot be cut into two
# windows of twelve, so its floor is the p95 movement between two 12-run medians drawn with
# replacement from it. Over those 24 runs, on the three rows computable both ways, that draw landed
# within a point of the reshuffle -- once narrower -- and on `images` about half again as wide, so
# it is the method a short population leaves rather than a systematically looser one. The checker
# refuses a new stamp under twenty-four runs beside a floor, so this one stands while its stamp
# does.
# `docs` gained two checks: `cell-prose` costs 0.05 s and `echo` 1.01 s over the whole corpus,
# measured locally on 2026-09-02 with the file listing already warmed, so the figures are the
# checks' own rather than the walk's.
# `docs` gained a third check: `scheme-token` costs 0.034-0.057 s over nine interleaved rounds with
# the file listing warmed, measured locally on 2026-09-05 on a sixteen-core machine carrying
# fourteen agent sessions, an editor and a browser, so the upper end reads that contention as much
# as the check. The second
# method resolves nothing and says so: the delta between a whole run carrying the check and one
# without falls inside that run's own 0.2 s spread, which is what a check this small looks like
# against a job this size. The ceiling it answers to is the `docs` row's budget, the total row
# carrying none behind it.
# `backend` gained a check: `check_test_estate.py` costs 6.28-7.53 s end to end over four runs, each
# returning exit 0, measured locally on 2026-10-06 over a tree of 199 test modules on a sixteen-core
# machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so both ends are upper bounds reading that contention
# as much as the check. It is pooled with the scope's other units, so the job pays that span only
# where the pool cannot start them all at once, and every run the `backend` row's stamp counts
# carries it.
# `docs` gained five checks -- `diagram`, `error-codes`, `invariant-number`, `output-verbs` and
# `wrapped-path` -- and widened two populations, the module-header scope to every file the hash
# reader answers for and the prose corpus by the notice file, with the fork-pool read behind the
# comment ceiling and the fork's standard behind the rule families. Measured whole rather than per
# check: the docs checker over the fork's tree and the branch's tree, interleaved, five rounds after
# one warm run each, on 2026-09-07 with nothing else running -- 7988 ms at the fork's median against
# 9267 ms at the branch's, spreads 16 ms and 59 ms, a difference of 1.3 s. The figures are one
# machine's upper bound; the runner's own spans are what the `docs` row's budget holds.
# `docs` gained a check: `check_public_routes.py` costs 110-129 ms end to end, of which 73 ms is the
# check rather than this interpreter's own start, over seven interleaved rounds after one warm run,
# each returning exit 0. Measured locally on 2026-09-07 on a sixteen-core machine carrying a fleet
# of concurrent agent sessions, so both ends are upper bounds reading that contention as much as
# the check. It is pooled with the docs scope's other units, so the job pays that span only where
# the pool cannot start them all at once.
# `db` gained a guard in front of the tier: a claim that refuses a second gate run rather
# than letting it run beside the first. Measured locally on 2026-09-07 over five interleaved rounds
# of two hundred iterations, on a Windows machine carrying a dozen agent sessions -- 22.6-26.5 ms to
# take the claim and 22.8-27.5 ms to give it back, both ends reading that machine's process spawn as
# much as the guard, and each paid once per run. Every run the `db` row's stamp counts carries the
# guard, so the budget cut from them already holds its 0.05 s. The figure is a development
# machine's, which is what the guard's own cost can be measured on: it runs before the tier rather
# than in it.
# `scripts`' binding unit measured three ways on 2026-09-07 on the sixteen-core machine: alone and
# idle, `selfcheck.sh` took 45.2-45.9 s over five runs; inside one full-form run it took 97 s beside
# the section's pytest, ruff and pyright; under a process spinning every core it took 236 s. The
# gap between alone and in-run is contention, the unit waiting on the machine rather than working,
# so what the row's budget holds is the run's figure and not the unit's, and what would pay is
# reducing what the run competes for rather than splitting the unit or removing work from it. The
# section itself binds the run at 122 s, its pytest unit the last to close; no figure here moves a
# row.
# `scripts`' pytest unit was one module long: `--dist loadfile` hands a module whole to one worker,
# and `scripts/tests/test_check_docs.py` carried 118.6 s of a 121.8 s run at eight workers against
# about 65 s of work a worker, while the case loop beside it, one test of 69 s, was dispatched last
# because xdist orders `loadfile` scopes by how many tests each holds. The net now stands in five
# modules, `scripts/tests/test_check_docs*.py`, and its cases one test apiece. Measured on
# 2026-09-22 on the sixteen-core machine at 100 per cent CPU from a fleet of agent sessions, three
# interleaved rounds of the whole suite in two mirrors of one tree, every run exit 0: the load moved
# each run's summed item time from 2378 to 3820 s, so the raw walls overlap; simulated on each
# new-layout run's own item times, which the simulation reproduces within 7 per cent, the old layout
# costs 649, 534 and 783 s against 466, 399 and 666 s. Read again on 2026-09-23 on the idle
# machine, two interleaved pairs of the whole suite at eight workers after one warm run of each: 93.0
# and 89.7 s on the old layout (729 cases) against 67.0 and 67.2 s on the new (773 cases, one of
# them failing on a job the file then had no row for), so the worst run after the split beats the
# best before it. No figure here moves a row.
# `docs` gained a check: `check_log_quoting_class.py` costs 97-141 ms end to end, of which about
# 60 ms is the comparison rather than this interpreter's own start, over two spreads of ten
# interleaved rounds after one warm run, each returning exit 0. Measured locally on 2026-09-07 on a
# sixteen-core machine carrying a fleet of concurrent agent sessions, so both ends are upper
# bounds reading that contention as much as the check. It opens two files and expands two
# character classes, so its span follows neither the size of the tree nor that of the branch. It is
# pooled with the docs scope's other units, so the job pays that span only where the pool cannot
# start them all at once.
# `docs` gained a check: `section-reference` costs 95-103 ms over the whole corpus of 1045 files,
# the upper end taken with the page cache cleared beside the check's own, over nine rounds
# interleaved with `wrapped-path`, which read 12 ms against the same corpus. Measured locally on
# 2026-09-07 on a sixteen-core machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so both ends are upper
# bounds reading that contention as much as the check, and the pages it resolves against are read
# once a run by the checks beside it either way. The same run widened the prose corpus by this file,
# 74 documents to 75.
# `docs` gained a check: `action-table` costs 59.5-63.9 ms over nine rounds, each in a fresh
# process with the file listing warmed and `error-codes` run first, as the gate orders them. Nine
# rounds interleaved with those, each calling it first, read 646.8-676.3 ms: the frontend source
# reads the two checks share, which the gate pays once. Measured locally on 2026-09-27 on a
# sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so both ends are upper bounds
# reading that contention as much as the check.
# `scripts` gained six cases: `scripts/tests/test_unit_shards.py` drives the gate's two shard
# refusals beside two cases reading the shard matrix, and `scripts/tests/test_regex_lead.py` lexes
# the regex-literal lead. Their calls cost at most 1.3-1.5 s together over three runs, a figure
# that also counted a case since cut, the two refusal cases 1.0 s of it, measured locally on 2026-09-23 on a sixteen-core Windows machine
# carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so both ends read that contention as much as the cases. The
# shard module is one chunk under `--dist loadfile` and the lexer's cases ride a module already
# dispatched, so the job pays that span only where the pool cannot start them beside the
# longest chunk.
# `frontend` gained forty test files rendering the editors through HeroUI on jsdom, and the five
# completed main push runs after they landed, 2026-09-19 to 2026-09-20, spanned 243, 260, 264, 268
# and 287 s first step to last. The unit tests are the whole
# move, 171 s on the runner against 35 s in the window before them, and the cost is each file's own
# process loading jsdom (1.05 s) and the HeroUI entry point (1.31 s) before a case runs, measured
# locally on 2026-09-19 on the sixteen-core machine: a file rendering nothing starts in 0.2 s and
# one rendering a rail in 2.9 s. Two levers were measured on that file over four interleaved rounds
# and rejected: Node's compile cache read slower than it saved, 3.8 s against 2.9 s, and dropping
# source maps altogether saves 0.25 s a file at the cost of every stack trace naming lines no file
# on disk holds. Both rejections stand: the compile cache re-measured on 2026-09-22 saved 4 percent
# of a rendering file's CPU with overlapping spreads, and the render harness maps the application's
# frames still, dropping only `node_modules`' (`fl_frontend/src/shared/testing/renderTest.ts`),
# whose frames no stack trace of ours reads.
# `fl_frontend/src/shared/testing/renderTest.ts` keeps each compiled component under
# `fl_frontend/node_modules/.cache/render-test`, keyed on its path and text, the harness and the
# installed TypeScript, and loads the compiler only on a miss. Over the whole unit suite, measured
# locally on 2026-09-23 on the sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions:
# 515.9-528.2 s of summed CPU in four runs without it, 443.6-494.2 s in four starting from an empty
# cache, which is every CI run, and 425.4-460.7 s in four with it filled, the failing-case set
# identical in each interleaved round. No budget moves and none takes a new stamp.
# `frontend-units` is one matrix job, and each of its instances is a row of its own under the name
# the job's `name:` template spells, which is the name the runs API reports and both the report and
# the budget check look a row up by. A row shared by the instances would have both readers fold
# names in step with each other, and the total would count one shard's span where every shard ran.
# Their four budgets are one figure, cut by the rule above from the widest shard span in the runs
# their stamp counts: `node --test --test-shard` hands a shard the files at its positions in the
# sorted list, whatever they cost, so which shard is heaviest moves as files are added.
# `scripts/checks/check_gate_budget.py :: check_matrix_budgets` refuses the four apart.
# `scripts` gained two cases: `scripts/tests/test_check_gate_budget.py` holds the `verify` job's
# `needs` to every other job in the workflow, and drives that reader over a job left out of it. They
# cost 0.546-0.593 ms a pass together over nine interleaved rounds in two runs, each case called
# directly rather than through pytest. Measured locally on 2026-09-23 on a sixteen-core Windows
# machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so both ends are upper bounds; the budget does not
# move and takes no new stamp.
# `scripts` gained thirteen cases in `scripts/tests/test_deploy_streams.py` judging the actor token's
# key pair, each spawning bash and two or three node processes, and its job now installs the
# application. The cases cost 12.2-48.0 s alone over three rounds interleaved with the rest of their
# module, which read 47.5-117.2 s against 11.8 s for the same 43 cases earlier that day, so the
# machine, not the cases, set most of that spread; the least-contended pair of whole-module runs puts
# them at 12-25 s. Measured locally on 2026-09-27 on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a fleet
# of agent sessions, so every figure is an upper bound, and the install and a Linux runner's process
# start are not measured here. The module is one chunk under `--dist loadfile`, so the job pays the
# cases only where that chunk becomes its longest. The budget does not move and takes no new stamp.
# `format` measured two ways of skipping the walk under `..`, which lists `fl_frontend/node_modules`
# and `.git` because prettier's own exclusions do not match there, and rejected both on their
# verdicts rather than their clocks. Prettier's fast CLI (`--experimental-cli`, prettier 3.9.6)
# checked the same files and passed a planted import-order swap the legacy CLI fails. Running the
# legacy CLI from the repository root, with `.prettierrc.json` naming its plugins by path, checked
# the same 1055 files and passed the same swap: prettier-plugin-tailwindcss runs the import sorter
# only when it can resolve that plugin by its package name, which it cannot from the root. Measured
# locally on 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-23 on a sixteen-core machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions.
# `db` gained the interleaved race cases and moved no figure. Two of them had parked a
# reopening at its first read of the referee, past its own write of the reopened fixture, so the
# erasure landing inside it waited out the transaction's sixty-second lifetime: 90 s and 73 s of a
# 185 s local run, and the runner's 208 s over this row's budget was the same wait. Parked at the
# reopening's first read of `spiele` the two take 0.08 s each, and the tier runs its 1113 cases in
# 21 s locally at width 6 on 2026-09-19, its slowest case 1.04 s.
# `docs` gained a rule: `check_tracked_text.py` refuses an invisible character beside a conflict
# marker, and that rule costs 60.9-62.1 ms over the corpus it already walks -- 1235 files read as
# text, 13.3 million characters -- against 686.7-705.6 ms for the conflict rule over the same corpus
# in the same process, the two arms interleaved across eight rounds. Measured locally on 2026-09-21
# on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions and an editor, so both ends
# are upper bounds reading that contention as much as the rule. The walk and the byte read are the
# checker's already, so that span is the whole marginal cost: one character-class scan answers a file
# holding none, which is nearly every file, and only a file with a hit is walked character by
# character.
# `frontend`'s unit tests were cut on 2026-09-22 by three changes to what each test file's process
# loads, measured as the summed CPU of every file's process on the sixteen-core Windows machine
# under a live fleet, over a frozen copy of HEAD, every run 292 files and 5131 passing cases:
# 834-896 s across five runs of the old `test` line against 518-533 s across two of the new one.
# Against the old line, the alias hook skipping TypeScript suffixes for a `node_modules`
# parent is about 5 percent, source maps for the application's modules alone about 6 percent, and a
# HeroUI or icon import loading only the names it takes, about 26 percent, a rendering file's
# process loading 2081 modules where it loaded 4160. Per-component subpath imports hold that now,
# loading the same modules within 40 in four of five sampled files; the fifth reaches
# `useOverlayState`'s root import.
# `db` gained the frontend's db-tier files (`pnpm run test:db`, each starting its own replica set
# through testcontainers) and the frontend toolchain step they need. Over the four files the branch
# holds, the tier took 40.8-41.7 s at a four-core runner's width of three files, against 39.6-40.4 s
# for the backend's db tier at its width of four, five interleaved rounds; the install behind them,
# `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` into an empty `node_modules` from a warm store, took 18.4-19.6 s
# over five runs. Where the scope runs alone, as its CI job does, it starts the two suites
# together (`scripts/gate/verify.sh :: start_steps`), the frontend's files spending their time
# waiting out the bounds they assert, and together they took 42.3-42.6 s in the same rounds, the
# longer suite and not the sum. Beside other scopes it runs them one after the other: in a bare
# gate run with every scope started together, the frontend's files took 129 s and six cases
# overran the sign-in store's 3 s bounds. Measured locally on 2026-09-26 on a sixteen-core Windows
# machine running nothing else. On a runner the `db` job spanned 140-149 s, median 144.5 s,
# every run over the row's budget, over the four pull-request runs of 2026-09-25 that ran the
# suites one after the other, and 90-114 s, median 99 s, over the thirteen pull-request and main
# runs from 2026-09-26 that start them together.
# `format`, `frontend`, the `frontend-units` shards and `db` gained a guard ahead of their
# scopes: `fl_frontend/node_modules` must exist, so a run without the install refuses rather than
# grading its absence. 58-60 microseconds a call over five interleaved rounds of two thousand calls
# against an empty loop, measured locally on 2026-09-23 on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying
# a fleet of agent sessions, so an upper bound; it is paid once in each gate process those scopes
# start. Every main run those jobs' budgets are cut from already paid it.
# `scripts` gained ten cases and lost eleven. `scripts/tests/test_pre_commit.py` commits through
# `.githooks/pre-commit` in fresh repositories, two on `main` and one on a branch, 1.26-1.34 s for the
# three; `selfcheck.sh` step 12's registration read, with its script missing and present,
# 0.43-0.45 s; `scripts/tests/test_gate_forms.py`'s pool-fallback notice, one gate run no pool
# serves and one the scope pool serves, beside the list of pooling scopes, 2.20-2.28 s with the
# module's fixture built afresh on every call; the launcher the two test tiers share and the shard matrix's one axis and count, under a
# millisecond each. Measured locally on 2026-09-23 over five rounds in rotated order, each case
# called directly, on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so every
# figure is an upper bound. The eleven cut --
# step 12's watchdog comparison, the two shard-matrix readers above and `job_names`' two samples --
# started no gate run. The budget does not move and takes no new stamp.
# `backend` gained a guard: `fl_backend/tests/tier.py :: TierGuard` watches every default-tier test
# through the driver's command listener, wrappers around each test's setup, call and teardown and
# around every fixture's setup, and a hook after each fixture's finalisation. The whole default tier
# took 49.8-55.6 s without it and 50.5-66.3 s with it, three interleaved rounds each in the gate's
# own serial form with `tests/core/test_tier.py` left out of both, the two quieter rounds putting
# the guard at 0.5-0.7 s. Measured locally on 2026-09-25 on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying
# a fleet of agent sessions, so both spreads are upper bounds. Every run the `backend` row's stamp
# counts carries the guard.
# `ops` traded three mirror checkers for one exposure check and a header block in the edge test.
# `nginx/edge_test.sh`, its header block now asking every location, took 3.21-3.33 s against
# 2.85-3.08 s for the redaction test alone, three interleaved rounds each, measured locally on
# 2026-09-23 on a sixteen-core machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so both ends are upper
# bounds. It sits inside the floor the `ops` row carries, and no row moves.
# `scripts` gained a module: `scripts/tests/test_pre_commit_format.py` commits through
# `.githooks/pre-commit` in fresh repositories, each case starting a real `node` through
# `.githooks/format-staged.mjs`. It took 38.0-41.2 s over five runs of the module alone, median
# 39.7 s, against 7.3-7.7 s for its six cases before the hook formatted the stage in one node
# process, interleaved, and the three cases holding the hook's refusal of a commit its own
# formatting emptied took 3.7-3.8 s of it. Measured locally on 2026-09-26 on the branch's tree of
# that night, on a sixteen-core Windows machine running nothing else, its processor under 4 percent
# before the series. `--dist loadfile` hands the module to one worker, where it is among the
# suite's longest chunks; the pytest unit's cost is recorded whole below.
# `scripts` gained a module: `scripts/tests/test_deploy_edge_config.py` drives the deploy's edge
# functions behind a stand-in `docker`, 10.0-10.7 s over three runs of the module alone against
# 5.8-6.0 s for `scripts/tests/test_deploy_streams.py` interleaved with it, measured locally on
# 2026-09-25 on a sixteen-core Windows machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, so an upper
# bound. It is shorter than the pre-commit module above. `ops` runs `nginx -t` over `nginx/prod/` mounted by directory, as
# production mounts it; the edge test mounts each file of `nginx/local/` by name beside its stub.
# `ops` gained a second nginx in the edge test, serving `nginx/prod/` behind a certificate made for
# the run so the www redirect is requested, a render of the local stack's model so the edge starts
# as compose starts it, a drive of its Control API, and a stand-in upstream sending a copy of every
# security header. The edge test took 8.4-8.7 s over five runs, median 8.4 s, against 3.7-4.9 s
# for the test before it, median 3.7 s, interleaved, measured locally on 2026-09-26 on the
# branch's tree of that night, on a sixteen-core Windows machine running nothing else. On
# 2026-09-25, with the same machine carrying a fleet of agent sessions, it took 9.2-10.1 s without
# the header copies and with them in the same rounds, so the copies cost less than that machine
# resolved. The scope also gained the two Compose renders, 459-494 ms each; `check_compose_model.py`
# over both, 155-164 ms end to end against 85-96 ms for the interpreter's own start, its
